subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should this issue be scoped to blocked-media diagnostics while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 or the `tools.fs.roots` work owns root expansion, or should this issue itself define a new accepted host-root policy?
rationale: The source bug is real, but accepting more absolute host paths changes a security-sensitive filesystem/media boundary and could create a competing config surface.

options.title: Diagnostics here, roots elsewhere
options.body: Keep this issue focused on clearer Telegram/media failure feedback and let the canonical configurable-root policy land through the existing root-policy tracker or approved filesystem-roots design.

options.title: Define root policy here
options.body: Use this issue as the policy vehicle for a supported configurable media-root contract, with schema, docs, security review, and upgrade tests.

options.title: Document as designed
options.body: Close or narrow the behavior as an intentional safe default that requires users to use managed roots or an existing file-read path.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics here, roots elsewhere
recommendation.body: Keep this issue focused on clearer Telegram/media failure feedback and let the canonical configurable-root policy land through the existing root-policy tracker or approved filesystem-roots design.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits closest to the outbound reply-media access policy commits he authored and maintained.
